event: United States and Israel begin strikes against Iran; the conflict starts.
source_note: UK House of Commons Library briefing
state_basis: Conflict-start warning state; this row is not presented as proof that the waterway was physically closed.

event: Iran asserts control over and restricts commercial passage through the Strait of Hormuz.
state_basis: Source-verified restriction/closure event; exact transition hour is not verified.

event: A two-week ceasefire agreement is reached.
state_basis: Ceasefire alone does not establish an open Strait, so it does not change the primary state.

event: United States begins a naval blockade of Iranian ports.
state_basis: Scope is Iranian ports; the source explicitly does not establish a general Strait closure.

event: United States and Iran reach an initial agreement to open the Strait and extend the ceasefire.
state_basis: RECODED (was included_primary=true, status=open): this is a diplomatic agreement-to-open, not a measured reopening. IMF PortWatch recorded 7-10 transits/day on 15-17 June (9-12% of the 81/day pre-conflict median baseline), below the 20% severely-restricted threshold. Excluded from primary state determination; the severely-restricted state continues until the independently observed 18 June transition.

event: JMIC advisory confirms that the Strait was open and blockade operations had ceased.
source_note: Joint Maritime Information Center via IMO
state_basis: RECODED (was status=open): PortWatch recorded 20 transits on 18 June, 24.7% of the 81/day pre-conflict baseline, inside the 20-70% restricted band rather than the >=70% open band. The advisory's own text says 'open_with_moderate_threat'; the word 'open' in the headline is not treated as a measured state here. Traffic stays in the 20-63% range through early July, so 'restricted' (a partial, contested corridor) is used, not 'open'.

event: Iran strikes three commercial vessels that had bypassed its Iran-approved transit route through the Strait, breaking down the June memorandum of understanding.
source_note: Al Jazeera conflict coverage; cross-checked against the Wikipedia-maintained List of ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war.
state_basis: NEW: source-verified attack event ending the partial-reopening window. PortWatch shows traffic falling from the 20-60% range of 18 June-4 July back toward single-digit percentages within days.

event: The June US-Iran memorandum of understanding collapses after the renewed attacks.
state_basis: NEW: corroborating annotation. Does not itself change the primary state, which already reverted to severely restricted on 6 July.

event: IRGC Navy declares the Strait of Hormuz closed until United States intervention in the region ends.
source_note: Iranian state media reporting the IRGC's own declaration; same sourcing tier as the CENTCOM-sourced US blockade rows.
state_basis: NEW: corroborating annotation of the general-Strait closure. Does not itself change the primary state, which already reverted to severely restricted on 6 July.

event: United States forces resume the naval blockade against Iran.
state_basis: RECODED (was status=open): scope is Iranian ports and non-general Strait transit, so this remains a sensitivity marker only, not a primary event. Status field updated from 'open' to 'severely_restricted' to match the recoded ongoing state (already severely restricted from the 6-12 July events), consistent with the 2026-04-07 ceasefire row's convention of describing the continuing state rather than the individual event's own character.
